text: 治承二年正月一日、院御所には拜禮行はれて、四日の日朝覲の行幸在けり。何事も例にかはりたる事は無れ共、去年の夏新大納言成親卿以下、近習の人々多く失れし事、法皇御憤未止ず、世の政も懶く思召されて、御心よからぬ事にてぞ在ける。太政入道も、多田藏人行綱が告知せて後は、君をも御後めたき事に思ひ奉て、上には事なき樣なれ共、下には用心して、苦笑てのみぞ在ける。

annotation.translation: On the first day of the first month of the second year of Jishō, a formal bowing ceremony was held at the Imperial Residence, and on the fourth day, an imperial visit for court audience took place. Although nothing was different from the usual customs, many of the close attendants, including the newly appointed Senior Counselor Narichika and others, had perished since the summer of the previous year; the Dharma Emperor's anger had not yet subsided, and he felt the government of the world to be sluggish, so his heart was not in good spirits. The Dajō-Dainagon (Retired Emperor) also, after receiving the report from Sadaijin no Kuramoto no Tsunetsuna, thought that he must show displeasure toward the Emperor; although outwardly everything seemed fine, inwardly he was on guard and could only offer a bitter smile.

text: 去程に入道相國の御女建禮門院、其比は未中宮と聞えさせ給しが、御惱とて、雲の上、天が下の歎にてぞ在ける。諸寺に御讀經始り、諸社へ官幣使を立らる、醫家藥を盡し、陰陽術を窮め、大法秘法一つとして殘る所なう修せられけり。され共、御惱たゞにも渡せ給はず、御懷姙とぞ聞えし。主上今年十八、中宮は二十二に成せ給ふ。然共、未皇子も姫宮も出來させ給はず。若皇子にてわたらせ給はば、如何に目出度からんと、平家の人々は唯今皇子御誕生の有樣に、勇悦びあはれけり。他家の人々も、「平氏の御繁昌折を得たり、皇子御誕生疑なし。」とぞ申あはれける。御懷姙定らせ給しかば、有驗の高僧貴僧に仰せて、大法秘法を修し、星宿佛菩薩につけて、皇子御誕生と祈誓せらる。六月一日、中宮御著帶有けり。仁和寺の御室守覺法親王、御參内有て、孔雀經の法をもて、御加持あり。天台の座主覺快法親王、同う參せ給て、變成男子の法を修せられけり。

annotation.translation: On the outward journey, the retired imperial consort, Lady Kensaimon-in, who at that time was said to be not yet Empress, was in a state of deep sorrow, lamenting as if she were above the clouds and beneath the heavens. She began reciting sutras in all temples, dispatched official envoys to all shrines, exhausted all medicines from physicians, and exhausted all Yin-Yang arts; not a single great dharma or secret dharma was left unpracticed. Yet, her sorrow was not dispelled, and it was said that she was pregnant. The reigning Emperor was eighteen this year, and the Empress had become twenty-two. Nevertheless, neither a prince nor a princess had been born. If she were to give birth to a prince, how joyous it would be, and the people of the Taira clan were filled with great joy and rejoicing at the prospect of the birth of a prince. The people of other households also said, "The Taira clan has now reached the height of its prosperity; there is no doubt that a prince will be born." Once her pregnancy was confirmed, she consulted with renowned and noble monks, practiced great and secret dharmas, and prayed and vowed to the stars, Buddhas, and Bodhisattvas for the birth of a prince. On the first day of the sixth month, the Empress wore a ceremonial sash. Prince Shukaku, the abbot of the imperial chamber at Ninnaji Temple, visited the inner palace and performed the ritual of the Peacock Sutra with its blessings. The abbot of Tendai, Prince Kakukai, also visited and practiced the ritual of transforming the fetus into a male.

text:
かゝりし程に、中宮は月の重るに隨て、御身を苦うせさせ給ふ。一度笑ば百の媚有けん漢の李夫人、昭陽殿の病の床もかくやと覺え、唐の楊貴妃、梨花一枝春の雨を帶び、芙蓉の風にしをれ、女郎花の露重げなるよりも猶痛しき御樣なり。かゝる御惱の折節に合せて、こはき御物怪共、取入奉る。よりまし明王の縛に掛て、靈顯れたり。殊には讃岐院の御靈、宇治惡左府の憶念、新大納言成親の死靈、西光法師が惡靈、鬼界島の流人共の生靈などぞ申ける。是によて太政入道生靈も死靈も、宥らるべしとて、其比やがて讃岐院御追號有て、崇徳天皇と號す。宇治惡左府、贈官贈位行はれて、太政大臣正一位を贈らる。勅使は少内記惟基とぞ聞えし。件の墓所は、大和國添上の郡、
河上の村、般若野の五三昧也。保元の秋掘起して捨られし後は死骸道の邊の土となて、
年々に只春の草のみ茂れり。今勅使尋來て、宣命を讀けるに、亡魂いかに嬉とおぼし
けん。怨靈はかく怖ろしき事也。されば早良の廢太子をば崇道天皇と號し、井上内親
王をば、皇后の職位に復す。是皆怨靈を宥められし策也。冷泉院の御物狂う坐し、花
山の法皇十善萬乘の定位をすべらせ給しは、基方民部卿が靈とかや。三條院の御目も
御覽ぜられざりしは、寛算供奉が靈也。

annotation.translation: As this went on, the Imperial Consort's body grew increasingly suffering with the passing of the moon. "Once she smiles, a hundred charms arise," so she recalled the Han dynasty's Lady Li, wondering if the bed of illness in the Zhaoyang Palace was like this. The Tang dynasty's Yang Guifei, bearing a branch of pear blossoms in the spring rain, withering in the wind of the lotus flower, was even more painful than the dew-laden lady's tassel. At this time of such suffering, the terrifying spirit-possessions approached and took hold. Having been bound by the fetters of the Vajradhara, they manifested their spiritual power. In particular, they mentioned the spirits of the Shikoku Emperor, the vengeful memories of the Uji no Akusa no Sakanefumi, the death-spirit of the newly appointed Dainagon Narichika, the evil spirit of Priest Saiko, and the living spirits of the exiles on the Island of the Ghost World. Because of this, the Dajō-daijin (Retired Emperor) was told that both his living and death spirits should be appeased. At that time, the Shikoku Emperor was posthumously given the title of Emperor Sutoku. The Uji no Akusa no Sakanefumi was posthumously granted official rank and title, receiving the posthumous title of Dajō-daijin, Shōichi-i. The imperial envoy was said to be the Shōnai-ki Tadamori. The said grave is in the Gun, Kawakami no Mura, Hannya no Gosanmai, in the Yamato Province. After it was dug up and abandoned in the autumn of the Hōgen period, the corpse became earth by the roadside, and only spring grass grew lush year after year. Now, the imperial envoy came searching, and when he read the imperial edict, the departed souls must have thought how joyful it was. Vengeful spirits are so terrifying. Therefore, the deposed Crown Prince of Saeki was posthumously titled Emperor Chūdo, and Princess Inoue was restored to the position of Empress. All these were strategies to appease the vengeful spirits. When Emperor Tsuchimikado suffered from madness, and Emperor Hanazono was able to attain the stable position of the Ten Goodness and Ten Thousand Vehicles, it was the spirit of Motokata, the Minister of the Department of the Household. When Emperor Sanjō did not even cast his eyes upon them, it was the spirit of Kansan, the attendant.

text: 門脇宰相か樣の事共傳聞いて、小松殿に申されけるは、「中宮御産の御祈樣々に候也。何と申候とも非常の赦に過たる事有るべし共覺え候はず。中にも鬼界島の流人共召還されたらん程の功徳善根、爭か候べき。」と申されければ、小松殿父の禪門の御前に坐て、「あの丹波少將が事を宰相の強ちに歎申候が不便に候。中宮御惱の御事、承及ぶ如くんば、殊更成親卿が死靈などと聞え候。大納言が死靈を宥んと思召んにつけても、生て候少將をこそ召還され候はめ。人の念ひを休させ給はば、思召す事も叶ひ、人の願を叶へさせ給はば、御願も既成就して中宮やがて、皇子御誕生有て、家門の榮花彌盛に候べし。」など被申ければ、入道相國、日來にも似ず事の外に和いで、「さて俊寛と康頼法師が事は、如何に。」「其も同う召こそ還され候はめ。若一人も留られむは、中中罪業たるべう候。」と申されたりければ、「康頼法師が事はさる事なれ共、俊寛は隨分入道が口入を以て、人と成たる者ぞかし。其に所しもこそ多けれ、我山莊鹿谷に城廓を構へて、事にふれて、奇怪の振舞共が有けんなれば、俊寛をば思もよらず。」とぞ宣ける。小松殿歸て叔父の宰相殿呼奉り、「少將は既に赦免候はんずるぞ。御心安う思召され候へ。」とのたまへば、宰相手を合てぞ悦ばれける。「下し時もなどか申請ざらんと思ひたり氣にて、教盛を見候度毎には涙を流し候しが、不便に候。」と申されければ、小松殿、「誠にさこそは思召され候らめ。子は誰とても悲ければ、能々申候はん。」とて入給ぬ。

annotation.translation: Hearing that the affairs of the Minister of the Left, Monokawa, had been reported, the Lord Komatsu said, 'It is a prayer for the Empress's childbirth, in various ways. Whatever one may say, there must be something that exceeds the bounds of extraordinary leniency, yet I am unaware of it. Especially the merit and good roots of summoning back the exiles from the island of Kikai; how could they be surpassed?' When he had said this, the Lord Komatsu sat before his father, the Archbishop, and said, 'It is inconvenient that the Minister of the Left has sighed loudly about the affair of the Minor Captain of Tango. If we can receive word of the Empress's distress, it will be heard that it is the dead spirit of Prince Narichika. Even if the Minister of the Great Council wishes to pacify the dead spirit of the Minister of the Great Council, it is the living Minor Captain who should be summoned back. If you would let people's thoughts rest, your wishes will be fulfilled; if you would let people's wishes be granted, your own wishes will already be fulfilled, and the Empress will soon give birth to a prince, and the glory and splendor of the family will become even more prosperous.' When he had said such things, the Imperial Retired Emperor, who had not been like himself in recent days, was extraordinarily at peace, and said, 'Well, what about the affairs of Shunkan and the monk Kōrai?' 'They too should be summoned back together. If even one is left behind, it will surely be a heavy sin,' he replied. 'The affair of the monk Kōrai is one thing, but Shunkan, through the earnest entreaties of the Imperial Retired Emperor, has become a person among men. Moreover, there were many reasons for this: in my mountain villa at Rokuhara, I built a castle, and whenever matters arose, strange and peculiar behaviors occurred; thus, I did not think of Shunkan.' When he had spoken thus, the Lord Komatsu returned and called upon his uncle, the Minister of the Left, saying, 'The Minor Captain has already been pardoned; please take heart.' When he said this, the Minister of the Left clasped his hands in joy. 'When I was granted permission, I thought, "Why would I not petition?" Yet, every time I saw Kyōmori, I shed tears, which was inconvenient,' he said. Then the Lord Komatsu replied, 'Truly, you must have thought thus. For a child, no matter who it is, is a cause of sorrow; I shall speak carefully,' and he departed.

text: 去程に鬼界が島の流人共召還るべく定められて、入道相國許文下されけり。御使既に都をたつ。宰相餘の嬉さに、御使に私の使をそへてぞ下されける。「夜を晝にして急ぎ下れ。」とありしか共、心に任ぬ海路なれば、浪風を凌いで行程に、都をば七月下旬に出たれ共、長月廿日比にぞ、鬼界が島には著にける。

annotation.translation: On the outbound journey, the exiles of Kikai Island were designated to be recalled, and the decree was issued from the Cloistered Prince, the Grand Minister. The imperial envoy had already departed the capital. The Grand Minister, filled with joy, ordered that his own messenger accompany the imperial envoy, saying, "Travel by day and night with haste." Yet, since the sea route could not be trusted, they braved the waves and wind; though they left the capital in the late July, they did not arrive at Kikai Island until the twentieth day of the eighth month.

text: 御使は丹左衞門尉基康と云者なり。船より上て「是に都より流され給し丹波少將殿平判官入道殿やおはする。」と、聲々にぞ尋ける。二人の人々は、例の熊野詣して無りけり。俊寛僧都一人殘りけるが、是を聞き、「餘に思へば夢やらん、又天魔波旬の我心を誑さんとて言やらん、現共覺ぬ物かな。」とて、周章ふためき走ともなく、倒るともなく、急ぎ御使の前に走り向ひ、「何ごとぞ、是こそ京より流されたる俊寛よ。」と名乘給へば、雜色が頸に懸させたる文袋より、入道相國の許文取出いて奉る。披いて見れば、「重科免遠流、早可成歸洛思。依中宮御産御祈被行非常赦。然間鬼界島流人少將成經、康頼法師赦免。」と計書かれて、俊寛と云文字はなし。禮紙にぞ有らんとて、禮紙を見るにも見えず。奧より端へ讀み、端より奧へ讀けれ共、二人と計書かれて、三人とはかゝれず。

annotation.translation: The messenger was a man named Tansaemon-no-jo Motoyasu. He climbed aboard and asked repeatedly, "Is it the Honorable Minister of Tanba, Taira no Gannokan Nyodo, or the Honorable Minister of Tanba, who was exiled from the capital?" The two men were, as usual, on a pilgrimage to Kumano. Only Shunkan Sogo remained. Hearing this, he thought, "If I think about it further, it must be a dream; or perhaps Mara, the Heavenly King, is speaking to deceive my mind; surely this is something not yet realized." He was in a panic, stumbling and running without direction, collapsing without intent, and hurriedly ran toward the messenger. When he said, "What is it? I am Shunkan, who was exiled from the capital," the messenger took out a letter from the bag of documents hanging around his neck, which had been entrusted by the Retired Emperor Sessho, and presented it. Upon opening and reading it, it stated: "A heavy punishment has been mitigated; it is now time to return to the capital. Because a special amnesty was granted in connection with the Empress's childbirth and prayers, the exiles of Oni-ga-jima, the Minister Naritsune and Priest Koryo, have been pardoned." There was no mention of the name Shunkan. He thought it must be a fake letter, but it did not look like one. He read it from the beginning to the end, and from the end to the beginning, but it was written as if for two people, not three.

text:
さる程に少將や判官入道も出來たり、少將の取てよむにも、康頼入道が讀けるにも、
二人と計かかれて、三人とはかゝれざりけり。夢にこそかゝる事は有れ、夢かと思ひ
なさんとすれば現也、現かと思へば又夢の如し。其上二人の人々の許へは、都より言
づけ文共、幾らも有けれ共、俊寛僧都の許へは、事問文一つもなし。さればわがゆか
りの物どもは都のうちにあとをとゞめず成りにけりとおもひやるにもしのびがたし。「抑我等三人は罪もおなじ罪、配所も一つ所也。如何なれば赦免の時、二人は召還されて、一人爰に殘るべき。平家の思忘かや、執筆の誤か。こは如何にしつる事共ぞや。」と、天に仰ぎ地に臥して、泣悲め共かひぞなき。少將の袂にすがて、「俊寛がかく成といふも、御邊の父、故大納言殿、由なき謀反故也。されば餘所の事とおぼすべからず。赦れ無れば、都迄こそ叶はずとも、此船にのせて、九國の地へ著けて給べ。各の是に坐つる程こそ、春は燕、秋は田面の雁の音信る樣に、自ら故郷の事をも傳聞つれ。今より後、何としてかは聞べき。」とて悶え焦れ給ひけり。少將、「誠にさこそは思召され候らめ。我等が召還るゝ嬉さは、去事なれ共、御有樣を見置奉るに、行べき空も覺えず。打乘奉ても上たう候が、都の御使も叶ふまじき由申す上、赦れも無に、三人ながら島を出たりなど聞えば、中々惡う候なん。成經先罷上て、人々にも申合せ、入道相國の氣色をも窺て、迎に人を奉らん。其間は此日比坐しつる樣に思成て待給へ。何としても命は大切の事なれば、今度こそ漏させ給ふ共、終にはなどか赦免なうて候べき。」と、慰め給へども、人目も知らず泣悶えけり。既に舟出すべしとて、ひしめきあへば、僧都乘ては下つ、下ては乘つあらまし事をぞし給ひける。少將の形見には夜の衾、康頼入道が形見には、一部の法華經をぞ留ける。纜解て押出せば、僧都綱に取附き、腰に成り、脇に成り、長の立つまでは引かれて出で、長も及ばす成ければ、船に取附き「さて如何に各、俊寛をば終に捨果給ふか。是程とこそ思はざりつれ。日來の情も今は何ならず。只理を枉て乘せ給へ。責ては、九國の地迄。」と口説かれけれ共、都の御使「如何にも叶ひ候まじ。」とて、取附給へる手を引のけて、船は終に漕出す。僧都せん方なさに、渚に上り倒伏し、少き者の乳母や母などを慕ふ樣に、足摺をして、「是乘て行け、具して行け。」と、喚叫べ共、漕行船の習にて、跡は白浪ばかりなり。未遠からぬ舟なれども、涙にくれて見えざりければ、僧都高き所に走あがり、澳の方をぞ招ける。彼松浦小夜姫が、唐舟を慕つゝ、領巾ふりけんも、是には過じとぞ見えし。船も漕隱れ、日も暮れ共、怪の臥處へも歸らず、浪に足打洗せ、露に萎て、其夜は其にてぞ明されける。さり共少將は情深き人なれば、能き樣に申す事も在んずらんと憑をかけ、其瀬に身をも投ざりける心の程こそはかなけれ。昔壯里息里が、海巖山へ放たれけん悲も、今こそ思ひ知られけれ。

annotation.translation: So it came to pass that the Shōshō and the Kanjō Nyūdō also arrived. Whether it was the Shōshō who took it upon himself to read, or the Kanjō Nyūdō who read it, both were plotted against, yet the three were not plotted against. Though such things may occur in dreams, if one thinks it must be a dream, it is real; if one thinks it is real, it is again like a dream. Moreover, though there were many letters and missives from the capital to the two men, not a single inquiry was sent to Shunkan Sōzu. Thus, thinking that all my cherished belongings have been left behind in the capital, it is unbearable. 'In the first place, the three of us share the same crime, the same place of exile. Why, then, at the time of pardon, are the two summoned back, leaving one here? Is this the negligence of the Taira clan, or a scribe's error? How could such a thing have happened?' Gazing upward to the heavens and lying prostrate upon the earth, he wept and wailed in vain. Clinging to the Shōshō's sleeve, he said, 'Even if Shunkan says it has come to this, it is because of the groundless rebellion of His Excellency the Great Minister, my late father. Therefore, it should not be regarded as a matter concerning others. If there is no pardon, even if I cannot reach the capital, please have me embarked on this boat and landed in the nine provinces. While we sit here, may we, like the swallows of spring and the geese of autumn fields, hear news from our native lands. From now on, how shall we ever hear of them?' Saying this, he was consumed with anguish and distress. The Shōshō replied, 'Truly, I am sure you think as you do. Though it is joyful that we are to be summoned, leaving you behind, I feel no desire to depart. Even if I were to board the boat and go to the capital, and the imperial messenger from the capital were to say that there is no pardon, and that all three of us have already been exiled to the islands, it would be exceedingly difficult. Konori has already departed; I shall speak with the people and also inspect the expression of the Nyūdō Sōkō to send someone to welcome you. In the meantime, please wait as if you were still sitting here on this day. Whatever the case, life is precious; though you may be spared this time, how can you ultimately be pardoned?' Saying this, he comforted him, yet Shunkan wept and writhed in anguish, unaware of the presence of others. When it was time to set sail, and they crowded together, the Sōzu boarded and disembarked, disembarked and boarded, performing all sorts of tricks. As a memento of the Shōshō, he left the night quilt; as a memento of Kanjō Nyūdō, he left a single chapter of the Lotus Sutra. When the rope was untied and the boat pushed off, the Sōzu clung to the rope, sat upon it, leaned against it, and was dragged out until his legs were straight, but since he could not reach the boat, he clung to the boat. 'Now, how will you ultimately abandon Shunkan? I never thought it would come to this. The affection of the past days is now gone. Just bend the law and take him aboard. If you do so, I will go as far as the nine provinces.' Though he was thus persuaded, the imperial messenger from the capital said, 'It is impossible in any way.' He pulled away the hand that held him, and the boat finally rowed away. With nowhere to turn, the Sōzu climbed ashore and fell prostrate, dragging his feet as if missing his young nurse or mother, shouting, 'Go on this boat, take this boat!' Yet, it was the custom of rowing boats, and all that remained behind was white foam. Though the boat was not far, he could not be seen through his tears. The Sōzu ran up to a high place and beckoned toward the inlet. Even the young Princess of Matsuura, longing for the Tang ships and waving her handkerchief, did not seem to surpass this. The boat rowed into concealment, the day grew dark, yet they did not return to the cave of the monsters; their feet were washed by the waves, their bodies withered by the dew, and that night was spent in such a state. Nevertheless, the Shōshō was a man of deep affection; he believed that he would surely say something appropriate, and so he cast himself into the swift current. How fleeting was the thought of his heart! Even the grief of Takazato and Ikariko when they were cast upon the sea rocks of Mt. Koyama is now fully understood.

text: 去程に此人々は、鬼界が島を出て、平宰相の領肥前國鹿瀬庄に著給ふ。宰相京より人を下して、「年の内は浪風も烈しう、道の間も覺束なう候に、それにて能々身いたはて、春に成て上り給へ。」とありければ、少將鹿瀬庄にて、年を暮す。

annotation.translation: On the outward journey, these people, having left the island of Oni-no-kai, arrived at Kashise-no-sho in Hizen Province, the domain of the Chancellor. Since the Chancellor had sent a messenger from Kyoto saying, 'Within the year the waves and winds are fierce, and the road is uncertain, so take good care of yourself and come up in spring,' the Shō no Shō spent the year at Kashise-no-sho.

text: さる程に同年十一月十二日の寅の刻より、中宮御産の氣坐すとて、京中六波羅ひしめきあへり。御産所は六波羅池殿にて有けるに法皇も御幸なる。關白殿を始め奉て、太政大臣以下の公卿殿上人、すべて世に人と數へられ、官加階に望をかけ、所帶所職を帶する程の人の、一人も漏るは無りけり。先例も、女御、后、御産の時に臨んで大赦行はるゝ事あり。大治二年九月十一日、待賢門院御産の時、大赦有りき。其例とて今度も、重科の輩多く許されける中に、俊寛僧都一人、赦免無りけるこそうたてけれ。

annotation.translation: Accordingly, on the twelfth day of the same year's eleventh month, from the hour of the Tiger, it was said that the Imperial Consort had given birth, and the capital of Kyoto was thronged with people. Although the place of childbirth was the Rokuhara Pond Mansion, the retired emperor also paid a visit. Beginning with the Dajokan, all the high-ranking nobles and courtiers from the Dajin no Daijin downward, all those counted among the people of the world, all those who aspired to official promotion and held some office or rank, not a single one was left out. It was also an established precedent that a general amnesty was proclaimed on occasions when a female consort or empress was about to give birth. In the second year of Taiji, on the eleventh day of the ninth month, there was an amnesty on the occasion of the Taimon-in's childbirth. On the grounds of this precedent, this time too, many offenders of serious crimes were pardoned, yet Shunken Sōzu alone was not granted clemency, which was most unjust.

text:
御産平安に在ならば、八幡、平野、大原野などへ、行啓なるべしと御立願有けり。仙源法印、是を敬白す。神社は太神宮を始奉て、二十餘箇所、佛寺は東大寺、興福寺、
已下十六箇所に御誦經あり。御誦經の御使は、宮の侍の中に、有官の輩是を勤む。平
紋の狩衣に帶劔したる者共が、色々の御誦經物、御劍御衣を持續いて、東の臺より南
庭を渡て、西の中門に出づ。目出たかりし見物なり。

annotation.translation: If the delivery proceeds safely, it is the Emperor's resolve to make a pilgrimage to Hachiman, Hirano, Oharano, and other places. Shingen Hoin respectfully reports this. For the shrines, beginning with the Taishingu, there are twenty-some locations; for the Buddhist temples, from Todaiji and Kofukuji downward, there are sixteen locations where the Emperor's chanting will be performed. The imperial messengers for the chanting are officials from among the palace attendants who perform this duty. Those dressed in plain-patterned kariginu with swords at their waists, carrying various chanting items, imperial swords, and imperial robes, cross from the eastern platform to the southern courtyard and emerge from the western central gate. It was a joyous sight to behold.

text: 小松大臣は例の善惡に噪がぬ人にて坐ければ、其後遙に程歴て、嫡子權亮少將以下公達の車共遣續させ、色々の御衣四十領、銀劔七つ、廣蓋に置せ、御馬十二匹引せて參り給。寛弘に上東門院御産の時、御堂殿御馬を參せられし其例とぞ聞えし。此大臣は中宮の御兄にて坐ける上、父子の御契なれば、御馬參せ給ふも理なり。五條の大納言國綱卿、御馬二匹進ぜらる。志の至か、徳の餘かとぞ人申ける。猶伊勢より始て、安藝の嚴島に至まで、七十餘箇所へ神馬を立らる。内裏にも寮の御馬に四手附て、數十匹引立たり。仁和寺御室は、孔雀經の法、天台座主覺快法親王は、七佛藥師の法、寺の長吏圓慶法親王は、金剛童子の法、其外五大虚空藏、六觀音、一字金輪、五壇の法、六字加輪、八字文殊、普賢延命に至るまで、殘所なう修せられけり。護摩の煙御所中にみち、鈴の音雲を響し、修法の聲身の毛堅て、如何なる御物のけなり共、面をむかふべしとも見えざりけり。猶佛所の法印に仰て、御身等身の藥師竝に五大尊の像を作り始らる。

annotation.translation: Minister Komatsu, being a man who did not make a fuss about the usual good and evil, sat there; and after a long time had passed, he ordered the carriages of the legitimate heir, the Crown Prince's attendant, and other courtiers to follow in succession, and had forty sets of various robes, seven silver swords, and wide umbrellas placed, and had twelve horses led to present them. It was heard that this was the same custom as when the Imperial Princess Go-Higashi-mon-in gave birth in the Kan'chō era, and the Imperial Palace horses were presented. This minister was the older brother of the Empress, and since they were father and son, it was only natural that he should present horses. The Great Counselor of the Fifth Ward, Lord Kunitaka, presented two horses. The people said, 'Is this the height of intention, or the abundance of virtue?' Moreover, from Ise all the way to Itsukushima in Aki, horses were stationed at more than seventy locations. Even within the Imperial Palace, four horses were attached to the stables of the various offices, and dozens of horses were led out. The Go-muro of Ninna-ji Temple practiced the Ritual of the Peacock Sutra; the Tendai Zushi Kakukai Hōshinnō practiced the Ritual of the Seven Buddhas Medicine Buddha; the head monk of the temple, Enkei Hōshinnō, practiced the Ritual of Vajra Child; and beyond these, the rituals of the Five Great Akashagarbhas, the Six Avalokiteśvaras, the One-Syllable Golden Wheel, the Five Altars, the Six-Syllable Golden Wheel, the Eight-Syllable Mañjuśrī, and the Universal Worthy Longevity were all performed without exception. The smoke of the homa filled the palace, the sound of the bells echoed in the clouds, the voice of the ritual made one's hair stand on end, and it seemed that no matter what supernatural phenomena might occur, one would not dare to turn one's face toward them. Furthermore, at the command of the Hōin of the Buddha's residence, images of the Medicine Buddha and the Five Great Honored Ones were made for their own bodies.

text:
かゝりしか共、中宮は隙なく頻らせ給ふばかりにて、御産も頓に成遣ず。入道相國、
二位殿、胸に手を置て、こはいかにせんとぞあきれ給ふ。人の物申しけれども、唯と
もかくも好樣にとぞ宣ける。さり共「軍の陣ならば、是程淨海は臆せじ物を。」とぞ
後には仰られける。御驗者は、房覺性運兩僧正、春堯法印、豪禪、實專兩僧都、各僧
伽の句どもあげ、本寺本山の三寶、年來所持の本尊達、責ふせ々々々もまれけり。誠
にさこそはと覺えて尊かりける中に法皇は、折しも新熊野へ御幸なるべきにて、御精
進の次なりける間、錦帳近く御座有て、千手經を打上遊されけるにこそ、今一際事替
て、さしも躍狂ふ御よりまし共が縛も、暫打靜けれ。法皇仰なりけるは、「如何なる
御物氣なり共、此老法師がかくて候はんには、爭か近附奉るべき。就中に今現るる所
の怨靈共は、皆我朝恩によて、人と成し者共ぞかし。縱報謝の心をこそ存ぜず共、豈
障碍を成すべきや。速に罷退き候へ。」とて女人生産し難からん時に臨で、邪魔遮障
し、苦忍難からんにも、心を致して大悲呪を稱誦せば、鬼神退散して、安樂に生ぜん
と遊いて、皆水精の御數珠を推揉せ給へば、御産平安のみならず、皇子にてこそ坐け
れ。

annotation.translation: Although things were like this, the Chunagon was constantly busy without any slack, and the childbirth was not yet accomplished. The Cloistered Emperor, the Dainagon, placing his hand on his chest, exclaimed in distress, 'How shall we manage this?' Though people offered various opinions, all agreed that such a situation was most fortunate. Yet later he declared, 'If this were a military camp, Kyo-kai would not be so timid.' The diviners were the two Sōjō, Bō Kakushō and Un, the Hōin Shun'gyō, Gōzen, and the two Sōzu, Jissen, each reciting verses from their respective monastic communities, and even the Three Treasures of the main temples and the principal images held over the years were rarely found to be so sternly demanding. Truly, one came to realize that such was indeed the case, and the dignity of the situation was profound. Meanwhile, the retired Emperor was about to make a pilgrimage to the new Kumano; as he was in the midst of his spiritual preparation, he was seated close to the brocade curtain and reciting the Thousand-Hand Sūtra. It was precisely then that the matter changed so drastically, and even his previously restless and frantic demeanor suddenly became calm. The Emperor declared: 'Whatever the nature of the spirit, how could an old monk like me approach it so boldly? Especially now, the vengeful spirits that have appeared are all those who, through the grace of our dynasty, have become human beings. Even if they harbor no gratitude or sense of repayment, how could they possibly create obstacles? Quickly, retreat!' Though people offered various opinions, all agreed that such a situation was most fortunate. Yet later he declared, 'If this were a military camp, Kyo-kai would not be so timid.' text: 頭中將重衡卿、其時は未中宮亮にておはしけるが、御簾の内よりつと出て、御産平安、皇子御誕生候ぞや。」と、高らかに申されければ、法皇を始參せて、關白殿以下の大臣、公卿、殿上人、各の助修、數輩の御驗者、陰陽頭、典藥頭、惣て堂上堂下、一同にあと悦あへる聲は、門外までどよみて、暫は靜りやらざりけり。入道餘りの嬉さに、聲をあげてぞ泣ける。悦泣とは是を云べきにや。小松殿、中宮の御方に參せ給て、金錢九十九文、皇子の御枕に置き、「天を以て父とし、地を以て母と定め給へ。御命は方士東方朔が齡を保ち、御心には天照大神入替らせ給へ。」とて、桑の弓蓬の矢を以て、天地四方を射させらる。

annotation.translation: The Chancellor Shigezane, who at that time had not yet been appointed to the position of Chamberlain, came forth hurriedly from within the curtain and loudly proclaimed, 'Is it true that the Imperial Consort's delivery is safe and that a Prince has been born?' With this, the Retired Emperor was the first to bow, and the Ministers, Privy Councillors, Court Nobles, and various attendants below, along with the numerable inspectors, the Chief of the Onmyo Bureau, the Chief of the Imperial Medical Bureau—all the court officials, both those above and below the hall—joined in a single, joyful outcry that echoed as far as the outer gates, and for a while there was no silence. Overwhelmed with joy as never before, he cried aloud. Could this be called 'joyful tears'? Lord Komatsu went to the side of the Imperial Consort and placed ninety-nine copper coins upon the Prince's pillow, saying, 'Let Heaven be your father and Earth your mother; may your life endure as long as the age of Fangshi Dongfang Shuo, and may the Sun Goddess Amaterasu take up residence within your heart.' Then, with a mulberry bow and mugwort arrows, he had the four directions of heaven and earth shot at.

text: 御乳には前右大將宗盛卿の北方と定められたりしが、去七月に難産をして失給しかば、御乳母平大納言時忠卿の北方、御乳に參せ給ひけり。後には帥典侍とぞ申ける。法皇軈て還御の御車を、門前に立られたり。入道相國嬉さの餘りに、砂金千兩、富士の綿二千兩、法皇へ進上せらる。然るべからずとぞ人人内々ささやきあはれける。

annotation.translation: Her wet nurse was designated to be the wife of the former Right Great General Shigemori, but since she died in July from difficult labor, the wife of the wet nurse, the Right Minister Tadatada, became her wet nurse. Later, she was called the Shun'i no Nyogo. The Dajō Daijin was greatly pleased, and offered to the Emperor a thousand taels of gold dust and two thousand taels of cotton from Mount Fuji. "This is not proper," people whispered to each other in their hearts.

text:
今度の御産に笑止數多あり。先法皇の御驗者、次に后御産の時御殿の棟より甑を轉かす事あり。皇子御誕生には南へ落し、皇女誕生には北へ落すを、是は北へ落したりければ、こは如何にと噪がれて取上て落なほしたりけれ共、惡き御事に人人申あへり。
をかしかりしは入道相國のあきれ樣、目出たかりしは小松大臣の振舞、本意なかりし
は前右大將宗盛卿の、最愛の北方に後れ奉て、大納言大將兩職を辭して籠居せられし
事、兄弟共に出仕あらば、如何に目出たからん。次に七人の陰陽師を召されて、千度
の御祓仕るに、其中に、掃部頭時晴と云ふ老者有り。所從なども乏少なりけり。餘に人多く參つどひて、たかんなをこみ、稻麻竹葦の如し。「役人ぞ、あけられよ。」とて、押分々々參る程に、右の沓を踏拔れて、そこにて些立休ふが、冠をさへ突落されぬ。さばかりの砌に、束帶正しき老者が、髻放てねり出たりければ、若き殿上人こらへずして、一度にどと笑ひあへり。陰陽師など云は、返陪とて足をもあだにふまずとこそ承れ。其に懸る不思議の有けるを、其時は何共覺えざりしか共、後こそ思合する事共も多かりけれ。御産によて、六波羅へ參らせ給ふ人々、關白松殿、太政大臣妙音院、左大臣大炊御門、右大臣月輪殿、内大臣小松殿、左大將實定、源大納言定房、三條大納言實房、五條大納言國綱、藤大納言實國、按察使資方、中御門中納言宗家、花山院中納言兼雅、源中納言雅頼、權中納言實綱、藤中納言資長、池中納言頼盛、左衞門督時忠、別當忠親、左宰相中將實家、右宰相中將實宗、新宰相中將通親、平宰相教盛、六角宰相家通、堀川宰相頼定、左大辨宰相長方、右大辨三位俊經、左兵衞督重教、右兵衞督光能、皇太后宮大夫朝方、左京大夫長教、太宰大貳親宣、新三位實清、以上三十三人、右大辨の外は直衣なり。不參の人々には、花山院前太政大臣忠雅公、大宮大納言隆季卿、已下十餘人、後日に布衣著して、入道相國の西八條の邸へ向はれけるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: There were many ridiculous occurrences in this recent childbirth. First, the former Emperor's spirit had a vision: when the Empress gave birth, a steamer was thrown from the ridge of the palace building. If a prince was born, it was dropped to the south; if a princess was born, to the north. Since it had been dropped to the north, people clamored, 'What is this?' and had it lifted and re-dropped, yet many still complained it was an ill omen. What was amusing was the bewildered expression of the Retired Emperor the State Chancellor; what was joyous was the conduct of the Minister Komatsu; what was regrettable was the case of the former Right Great General Lord Morimori, who, falling behind his beloved consort, resigned both the posts of Great Minister and Great General and withdrew into seclusion. If both brothers had taken up their posts, how joyous it would have been! Next, seven Onmyoji were summoned to perform a thousandfold purification. Among them was an old man named Tokiharu, the Kanmon-no-tayu. His attendants and such were scanty. However, many other people gathered, crowding the place like rice, hemp, bamboo, and reeds. 'Let the officials clear the way!' they shouted, and as they pushed through one by one, the right shoe was pulled out from under him, and he was forced to stop and rest there, yet even his cap was not knocked off. In such a situation, an old man wearing a proper court robe suddenly let down his topknot and emerged, and the young courtiers could not hold back, bursting into laughter all at once. The Onmyoji and others said, 'When returning, one should not even lightly place the feet.' Though at the time one could not perceive the strangeness involved, later there were many things one came to understand. As for those who were sent to Rokuhara due to the childbirth, they were: the Kampaku, Lord Matsudono; the Dajō-daijin, Myōon-in; the Sadaijin, Ōgimi-no-mon; the Udaijin, Tsukinowa-dono; the Naidaijin, Komatsu-dono; the Left Great General Sadamori; the Gen Dainagon Sadafusa; the Sanjō Dainagon Sanefusa; the Gojō Dainagon Kunitsuna; the Fujiwara Dainagon Sanekuni; the Anjatsushi Sukekata; the Nakamikado Chunagon Munekage; the Hanazono-in Chunagon Kanemasa; the Gen Chunagon Masayori; the Gon Chunagon Sanetsuna; the Fujiwara Chunagon Sukehisa; the Ikeda Chunagon Yorimori; the Saemon-no-suke Tokitada; the Betto Tadahisa; the Saishō-shō Chunagon Sanekage; the Usō-shō Chunagon Masamune; the Shin Shō-shō Chunagon Michitomo; the Hira Shō-no-suke Norimori; the Rokkaku Shō-no-suke Iemichi; the Horikawa Shō-no-suke Yorisada; the Sa-dai-ben Shō-no-suke Nagakata; the U-dai-ben no Sanmi Shunetsugu; the Sa-hei-no-suke Shigenori; the U-hei-no-suke Mitsunori; the Kōtai-gū no Daifu Asamasa; the Sa-kyō no Daifu Nagatsugu; the Dazaishō no Dai-ni Chikatsune; the Shin Sanmi Sanekiyoshi. Altogether thirty-three persons, all wearing jōgi except the Right Great Minister. As for those who did not attend, there were the Hanazono-in Former Dajō-daijin Lord Tadayoshi, the Ōmiya Dainagon Takasuke, and more than ten others below them; it was heard that on a later day they donned plain robes and went to the Western Hachijō residence of the Retired Emperor the State Chancellor.

text:
御修法の結願には、勸賞共行はる。仁和寺の御室は東寺修造せらるべし。並に後七日の御修法、大元の法、灌頂興行せらるべき由仰下さる。御弟子覺誓僧都、法印に擧せらる。座主の宮は、二品竝に牛車の宣旨を申させ給ふ。仁和寺の御室さゝへ申させ給ふによて、法眼圓良、法印に成さる。其外の勸賞共毛擧に遑あらずとぞ聞えし。中宮は日數經にければ、六波羅より内裏へ參せ給ひけり。此御娘、后に立せ給しかば、入道相國夫婦共に、「哀れ、如何にもして皇子御誕生あれかし。位に即奉て、外祖父、
外祖母と仰れん。」と願ける。我が崇奉る安藝の嚴島に申さんとて、月詣を始て、祈
り申されければ、中宮やがて、御懷姙有て、思ひのごとく皇子にて坐けるこそ目出度
けれ。

annotation.translation: Upon the completion of the Great Ritual, the Emperor and the Empress Dowager both proceeded. The Imperial Chamberlain of Ninna-ji Temple was to have the Tō-ji Temple repaired. Furthermore, it was decreed that the Great Ritual of the Seven Days after death, the Great Dharma, and the consecration ceremony should be conducted. The Imperial Disciple Kakushō Sōzu was promoted to Hōin. The Temple Abbot was granted the Imperial Edict to be promoted to the rank of Second Rank and to ride in a two-horse carriage. By having the Imperial Chamberlain of Ninna-ji Temple present his recommendation, the Hōgen Engyō became Hōin. It was reported that the Emperor and Empress Dowager had no hesitation in promoting the others. Since the time elapsed was long, the Imperial Consort traveled from Rokuhara to the Imperial Palace. When this Imperial Daughter was established as Empress, the Cloistered Emperor and the Cloistered Chancellor both prayed, 'How pitiable! Let us pray that a prince be born. Upon his ascension to the throne, may we be called his maternal grandfather and maternal grandmother.' As they had begun monthly pilgrimages to pray, saying they would offer their devotion at the revered Itsukushima Shrine in Awa, the Imperial Consort soon became pregnant, and the birth of a prince as wished was indeed a cause for great joy.

text:
抑平家安藝の嚴島を信じ始られける事は如何にと云に、鳥羽院の御宇に清盛公未安藝守たりし時、安藝國を以て、高野の大塔を修理せよとて、渡邊遠藤六郎頼方を雜掌に附られ、六年に修理畢ぬ。修理畢て後、清盛高野へ上り、大塔拜み、奧院へ參られたりければ、何くより來る共なき老僧の、眉には霜を垂れ、額に浪を疊み、鹿杖の兩股なるにすがて、出來給へり。稍久しう御物語せさせ給ふ。「昔より今にいたる迄此れは密宗をひかへて退轉なし。天下に又も候はす。大塔既に修理終候たり。さては、安藝の嚴島、越前の氣比の宮は、兩界の垂跡で候が、氣比の宮は榮たれ共、嚴島はなきが如くに荒果て候。此次に、奏聞して修理せさせ給へ。さだにも候はば、官加階は肩を竝ぶる人、有まじきぞ。」とて立れけり。此老僧の居給へる所に異香薫じたり。人を附て見せ給へば、三町許は見給て其後は掻消すやうに失せ給ぬ。是唯人には非ず。
すなはち大師にて坐けりと、彌々尊く思召し、娑婆世界の思出にとて、高野の金堂に曼陀羅を書かれけるが、西曼陀羅をば、常明法印といふ繪師に書せらる。東曼陀羅をば、清盛書んとて、自筆にかゝれけるが、何とかおもはれけん、八葉の中尊の寶冠をば我首の血を出いて、書かれけるとぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: Now, as for why the Taira were to believe in the Itsukushima Shrine of Awa Province, it is said as follows: During the reign of the Emperor Toba, when Kiyomori was still the Governor of Awa, he was ordered to repair the Great Stupa of Mount Koya by dedicating the province of Awa for that purpose. Thus, Watanabe Endo Rokuro Yorikata was appointed as a lay attendant, and the repair was completed in six years. After the repair was finished, Kiyomori ascended to Mount Koya, paid his respects to the Great Stupa, and entered the inner sanctum. There, an old monk appeared, seemingly from nowhere, with frost hanging from his eyebrows, waves of wrinkles on his forehead, leaning on a deer-staff, and looking quite aged. After a while, he was asked to tell a story. He said, 'From ancient times until now, this has been the secret of the Esoteric School, and there has been no apostasy. It is destined to happen once more in the world. The Great Stupa has already been repaired. Therefore, the Itsukushima Shrine of Awa Province and the Kibi Shrine of Echizen Province are manifestations of the two worlds. While the Kibi Shrine has flourished, the Itsukushima Shrine has become desolate as if it were abandoned. In this instance, I request that you submit a report to the Emperor and have it repaired. If you truly intend to do so, you will not lack the opportunity for official promotion, as there are many people who will stand shoulder to shoulder with you.' Saying this, he stood up. A strange fragrance filled the place where the old monk had been seated. When people were sent to investigate, they saw it for about three cho, after which it vanished as if erased. This was not merely a human being. It was none other than Kobo Daishi himself, who sat there. They thought of him with even greater reverence and, to create a memory of the Saha World, had a mandala painted in the Golden Hall of Mount Koya. The Western Mandala was painted by a painter named Jomyo Hoin, while Kiyomori intended to paint the Eastern Mandala himself and began to work on it with his own brush. However, it is said that he somehow thought, 'I will shed the blood from my head to paint the jewel crown of the central figure in the eight-petaled mandala.'

text:
さて都へ上り、院參して、此由奏聞せられければ、君もなのめならず御感有り。猶任を延られて、嚴島を修理せらる。鳥居を立替へ、社々を造りかへ、百八十間の廻廊をぞ造られける。修理畢て、清盛嚴島へ參り、通夜せられたりける夢に、御寶殿の
内より、鬟結たる天童の出て、「是は大明神の御使なり。汝此劔を以て一天四海をし
づめ、朝家の御まもりたるべし。」とて、銀の蛭卷したる小長刀を賜ると云夢を見て、
覺て後見給へば。現に枕上にぞ立たりける。大明神御託宣有て、「汝知れりや忘れり
や、或聖を以て言せし事は。但惡行有らば、子孫迄は叶ふまじきぞ。」とて、大明神
あがらせ給ぬ。目出度かりし御事なり。

annotation.translation: Now, he ascended to the capital, paid a visit to the retired emperor, and since this was reported to the emperor, the Lord was not displeased but felt grateful. Furthermore, he was entrusted with the task of repairing Itsukushima. The torii gate was replaced, the shrines were rebuilt, and a corridor 180 ken in length was constructed. Upon completion of the repairs, Kiyomori visited Itsukushima. In a dream during the all-night vigil, a heavenly boy with a topknot emerged from within the main hall and said, 'This is the messenger of the Great Deity. With this sword, you shall calm the four seas and protect the Imperial House.' He was then granted a small long sword with a silver hilt. Upon waking and looking around, he saw that the sword was indeed standing by his pillow. The Great Deity delivered a divine oracle: 'Do you remember or have you forgotten what was said through a certain sage? If there are evil deeds, it will not be granted even to your descendants.' Thus, the Great Deity ascended to heaven. What a joyous event it was.

text: 白河院御在位の御時、京極大殿の御娘の后に立せ給て、賢子の中宮とて、御最愛有けり。主上此御腹に、皇子御誕生あらまほしう思召、其比、有驗の僧と聞えし三井寺の頼豪阿闍梨を召て、「汝此后の腹に、皇子御誕生祈り申せ、御願成就せば、勸賞はこふによるべし。」とぞ仰ける。「安う候」とて三井寺に歸り、百日肝膽を摧て祈申されければ、中宮軈て百日の内に御懷姙有て、承保元年十二月十六日。御産平安、皇子御誕生有けり。君なのめならず御感有て三井寺の頼豪阿闍梨を召て、「汝が所望の事は如何に。」と仰下されければ、三井寺に戒壇建立の事を奏す。主上「是こそ存の外の所望なれ。一階僧正などをも申べきかとこそ思召つれ。凡は皇子御誕生有て、皇祚を繼しめん事も、海内無爲を思ふ爲なり。今汝が所望達せば、山門憤て、世上も靜なるべからず。兩門合戰して、天台の佛法亡なんず」とて、御許されも無りけり。

annotation.translation: During the reign of Emperor Shirakawa, the Great Lord of the Imperial Court [Konoe] had his daughter installed as empress, and she was known as Empress Kenko, whom he loved dearly. The Emperor, desiring that a prince be born from her womb, summoned Ryōgō Shōnin of Miidera, who was known as a monk of great efficacy, and said, 'Pray that a prince be born from your womb; if your wish is granted, I shall reward you generously.' He replied, 'Very well,' and returned to Miidera. After praying with all his heart for one hundred days, the Empress became pregnant within that hundred-day period. On the 16th day of the 12th month of the first year of Shōei, she gave birth safely, and a prince was born. The Emperor was so moved that he summoned Ryōgō Shōnin of Miidera and asked, 'What is your desire?' Ryōgō Shōnin then petitioned for the establishment of a kaidan (ordination platform) at Miidera. The Emperor replied, 'This is indeed a wish beyond my expectation. I was even considering appointing you as a senior priest of the first rank. In general, the birth of a prince and the continuation of the imperial line are for the sake of bringing peace to the land. If your wish is granted, the two temples will become angry, and the world will not be quiet; the Tendai and Tōdai schools will fight, and the Buddhist Dharma of Tendai will perish.' Thus, he did not grant his permission.

text: 頼豪口惜い事なりとて、三井寺に歸て、干死にせんとす。主上大に驚かせ給て、江帥匡房卿其比は未美作守と聞えしを召て、「汝は頼豪と師檀の契有なり。行いて拵て見よ。」と仰ければ、美作守綸言を蒙て、頼豪阿闍梨が宿坊に行向ひ、勅定の趣を仰含んとするに、以の外にふすぼたる持佛堂に立籠て、怖氣なる聲して、「天子には戯の言なし、綸言汗の如しとこそ承れ。是程の所望叶はざらんに於ては、我祈出したる皇子なれば、取奉て魔道へこそ行んずらめ。」とて、遂に對面も爲ざりけり。美作守歸り參て、此由を奏聞す。頼豪は軈て干死に死けり。君如何せんずると叡慮を驚させおはします。皇子やがて御惱附せ給て、樣々の御祈共有しかども、叶ふべし共見えさせ給はず。白髮なりける老僧の、錫杖を以て、皇子の御枕に彳み、人々の夢にも見え、幻にも立けり。怖なども愚也。

annotation.translation: Rengo said, 'It is a grievous matter,' and returned to Miidera, intending to starve himself to death. The Emperor was greatly alarmed and summoned Shōsai Masafusa, who at that time was known as Mimasaka-no-mori. He said, 'You have a teacher-disciple bond with Rengo. Go and try to persuade him.' Upon receiving this imperial decree, Mimasaka-no-mori went to Rengo's lodging to convey the emperor's intentions. However, Rengo, who was extremely stubborn, locked himself inside his small prayer hall and, in a terrifying voice, declared, 'The Emperor does not speak in jest; the imperial decree is as certain as sweat. Since this is the son I prayed for, if my wish is not fulfilled, I shall surely go to the path of the demons.' Thus, he refused to meet even once. Mimasaka-no-mori returned and reported these circumstances. Rengo ultimately died of starvation. The Emperor, deeply troubled by this, pondered what could be done. The prince soon felt sorrowful, and although various prayers were offered, no relief seemed possible. The old monk, with white hair, struck the prince's pillow with his staff, appearing in people's dreams and visions. Fear is nothing but folly.

text: 去程に承暦元年八月六日、皇子御年四歳にて遂に隱させ給ぬ。敦文の親王是也。主上斜ならず御歎有けり。山門に又西京の座主、良信大僧正、其比は圓融坊の僧都とて有驗僧と聞えしを内裏へ召て、「こは如何せんずる。」と仰ければ、「何も、吾山の力にてこそか樣の御願は成就する事で候へ。九條右丞相、慈慧大僧正に契申させ給しに依てこそ、冷泉院の皇子御誕生は候しか。安い程の御事候。」とて、比叡山に歸り上り、山王大師に、百日肝膽を摧て祈申ければ、中宮軈て百日の内に御懷姙有て、承暦三年七月九日、御産平安、皇子御誕生有けり。堀川の天皇是なり。怨靈は昔もかく怖しかりし事也。今度さしも目出度き御産に、非常の大赦行はれたりといへ共、俊寛僧都一人、赦免無りけるこそうたてけれ。

annotation.translation: On the outward journey, on the sixth day of the eighth month of the first year of Jōchō, the imperial prince, aged four, was finally hidden away. This was Prince Atsunofu. The reigning emperor was not displeased, yet he sighed. At the mountain temple, once again, the abbot of the Western Capital, the Great Priest Ryōshin, who at that time was known as the Priest Sūri of Enryūbō and was reputed to be a priest of great efficacy, was summoned to the inner palace. When he was told, 'What shall be done about this?' he replied, 'Nothing, but with the power of our mountain, such an imperial wish shall be fulfilled. It was because the Right Minister of the Ninth Ward, the Great Priest Jie, had made a contract with the Great Priest Jie, that the birth of the imperial prince of the Reizei-in occurred. It is a matter of such a trivial nature.' Thus he returned to Hieizan, ascended to the mountain, and, with his liver and gall destroyed in prayer for a hundred days before the Great Master of the Mountain King, the imperial consort, within a hundred days, became pregnant, and on the ninth day of the seventh month of the third year of Jōchō, she gave birth safely, and the imperial prince was born. This was the Emperor of Horikawa. Such were the fearful powers of vengeful spirits in the past. Although a great general amnesty was issued on this occasion, for the joyous birth, yet for Shunkan, the priest Sūri alone, there was no pardon, which was most grievous.

text: 同十二月八日。皇子東宮に立せ給ふ。傅には、小松内大臣、大夫には池中納言頼盛卿とぞ聞えし。

annotation.translation: On the eighth day of the twelfth month of that year, the imperial prince was established as Crown Prince. As his tutor was the Minister of the Left Komatsu, and as his tutor of the palace was the Chamberlain of the Center Yoritomo of the Ike-no-Tsu, so it was heard.

text:
明れば治承三年正月下旬に丹波少將成經、肥前國鹿瀬庄を立て、都へと急がれけれ共餘寒猶烈しく、海上も痛く荒ければ、浦傅島傅して、きさらぎ十日比にぞ、備前の兒島に著給ふ。其より父大納言殿の住給ける處を尋いりて見給ふに、竹の柱、舊たる障子なんどに書置れたる筆のすさびを見給て、「人の形見には手跡に過たる物ぞなき。
書置給はすば、爭か是を見るべき。」とて、康頼入道と二人、讀では泣き、泣いては
讀む。「安元三年七月廿日出家、同廿六日、信俊下向。」とも書かれたり。さてこそ
源左衞門尉信俊が參りたりけるも知れけれ。そばなる壁には、「三尊來迎便有り、九
品往生疑なし。」とも書かれたり。此形見を見給てこそ、「さすが欣求淨土の望も御
座けり。」と、限なき歎の中にも、聊頼しげには宣けれ。

annotation.translation: In the late February of the third year of Jishō, the Tamba no Shōjō Naritoki set out from Kashima-shō in Hizen Province, hastening toward the capital; however, the lingering cold was still severe, and the sea was rough and stormy, so he made his way by boat from port to port, and on the tenth day of Kisaragi, he arrived at Kojima in Bizen. From there, seeking the residence of his father, the Dainagon, he looked upon it and saw the handwriting of his father preserved on the bamboo pillars and the old sliding doors. He said, 'There is nothing that surpasses a person's handwriting as a memento. I would be grateful to see it,' and he and the monk Kōrai read it, weeping as they read, and reading as they wept. It was written: 'On the 20th day of the 7th month of the third year of An'gen, he took vows as a monk; on the 26th of the same month, he went to Shōshun.' Thus it became known that the Genzaemon no Tō Shōshun had indeed come. On the nearby wall was also written: 'The Threefold Coming of the Buddha is certain; there is no doubt about birth in the nine grades of the Pure Land.' Seeing this memento, he exclaimed, 'Truly, there is hope for the longing of the Pure Land.' Even amidst endless sighs, he spoke with a faint semblance of hope.

text: 其墓を尋て見給へば、松の一村ある中に、甲斐々々しう壇を築たる事もなし。土の少し高き所に少將袖掻合せ、生たる人に申樣に、泣々申されけるは、「遠き御守と成せ御座して候事をば、島にて幽に傳へ承しか共、心に任せぬ憂世なれば、急ぎ參る事も候はず。成經彼島へ流れて露の命の消やらずして、二年を送て、召還さるる嬉さは、さる事にて候へ共、此世に渡せ給ふを見參て候はばこそ、命の長きかひもあらめ。是までは急がれつれ共、今日より後は、急ぐべし共覺えずと、掻口説てぞ泣かれける。誠に存生の時ならば、大納言入道殿こそ、如何に共宣ふべきに、生を隔たる習程、恨めしかりける物はなし。苔の下には誰か答ふべき。唯嵐に騒ぐ松の響計也。

annotation.translation: If you search for his grave, you will find that within a grove of pines there is not even a mound built with any semblance of dignity. On a slightly raised spot of earth, the sleeves of the Minor Counselor are joined, as if to a living person, and with tearful entreaties it was said: 'Though you quietly conveyed the matter on the island, that I might become your long-term guardian, since the world is filled with sorrow beyond control, I have not hastened to come. When Naritsune was exiled to that island, the joy of returning while his life of dew remained unextinguished after spending two years was, though such a thing, but to have seen you cross over to this world would surely have been the meaning of a long life. Until now, though I was hurried, from today onward, though I should hasten, I do not feel able to, and thus with coaxing words he was wept over. Truly, if he were still alive, the Great Counselor the monk would surely have said something in some manner, but since it is the custom to be separated by life, there was nothing more regrettable. Who could answer beneath the moss? Only the sound of pines rustling in the storm.'

text: 其後はよもすがら康頼入道と二人、墓の廻を行道して念佛申し、明ぬれば新う壇築き、釘貫せさせ、前に假屋作り、七日七夜、念佛申し經書て結願には大なる卒塔婆を立て、「過去聖靈出離生死、證大菩提」と書て、年號月日の下に、「孝子成經」と書かれたれば、賤山賤の心無も、子に過たる寶はなしとて、涙を流し、袖を絞ぬは無りけり。年去年來れ共、忘難きは撫育の昔の恩。夢の如く幻の如し。盡難きは戀慕の今の涙なり。三世十方の佛陀の聖衆も憐み給ひ、亡魂尊靈も、如何に嬉しと覺しけん。「今暫候て、念佛の功をも積べう候へ共、都に待つ人共も心元なう候らん。又こそ參候は。」とて、亡者に暇申つゝ、泣々そこをぞ立れける。草陰にても名殘惜うや思はれけん。

annotation.translation: Thereafter, throughout the night, he and the monk Kōrai walked around the grave, reciting the Nembutsu. When morning came, they built a new altar, drove in nails, constructed a temporary hut in front, and for seven days and seven nights recited the Nembutsu and sutras. To conclude the vows, they erected a great stupa inscribed with the words 'May the spirits of the departed be liberated from birth and death and attain Great Enlightenment.' Below the date and year, they wrote 'Filial son Narifusa.' Seeing this, even a heart as base and low as that of Senzan, he thought, 'There is no treasure greater than a child,' and shed tears, wringing out his sleeve until it was dry. Year after year passed, yet it was difficult to forget the kindness of the days when he was nurtured. It was like a dream, like an illusion. What was most difficult to bear were the tears of longing in the present. Even the holy hosts of Buddhas in the three times and ten directions must have felt compassion; how joyful must the departed spirit have felt! 'Though I shall remain here for a while and accumulate the merit of the Nembutsu, surely those waiting in the capital are growing anxious. I must visit them once more,' he said, bidding farewell to the deceased, and then, weeping, he rose from that spot. Even in the shade of the grass, one wonders if they felt a lingering reluctance.

此古き詩歌を口ずさみ給へば、康頼入道も折節哀に覺えて、墨染の袖をぞ濕しける。
暮る程とは待れけれ共、餘に名殘惜くて、夜更る迄こそ坐けれ。更行まゝに、荒たる
宿の習とて、古き軒の板間よりもる月影ぞ隈もなき。鷄籠の山明なんとすれ共、家路
は更に急がれず。さてしも有べき事ならねば、迎に乘物ども遣て、待らんも心なしと
て、泣々洲濱殿を出つゝ、都へ歸り入給けん人々の心の中共、さこそは哀にも嬉しう
も有けめ。康頼入道が迎にも乘物有けれ共其には乘らで、「今更名殘の惜に。」とて、
少將の車の尻に乘て、七條河原までは行く。其より行別れけるに、猶行もやらざりけ
り。花の下の半日の客、月の前の一夜の友、旅人が一村雨の過行に、一樹の陰に立よ

annotation.translation: When he chanted this ancient poem, Kōrai the Priest also, at that very moment, felt a deep sorrow and wetted his sumizome-dyed sleeves. Though he had said he would wait until dusk, he was so reluctant to part that he sat until late at night. As he continued to walk, the custom of this dilapidated inn being a place of old eaves and moonlight streaming through the gaps became apparent. Though the rooster's cage suggests dawn is near, he did not hasten his journey home. Since it was not possible to do otherwise, he sent for the carriages to meet him, thinking there was no point in waiting, and as he left the residence of the crying shores, among the hearts of those returning to the capital, surely they felt both sorrow and joy. Although Kōrai the Priest had carriages ready for him, he did not ride in them, saying, 'Now, more than ever, I am reluctant to part,' and instead rode at the rear of the Minor Captain's carriage as far as Shichijō Riverbank. There, when they parted ways, he still did not proceed further. A guest beneath the flowers for half a day, a friend before the moon for one night, a traveler stopping under the shadow of a single tree as a passing rainstorm moves through a village—how sorrowful the lingering parting! And indeed, this is a dwelling on the island of sorrow, a body within a boat, upon the waves, a person of a single moment's emotion; surely the fragrance of a past life's bond must have been deeply felt.

text: 少將は舅平宰相の宿所へ立入給ふ。少將の母上は、靈山に坐けるが、昨日より宰相の宿所に坐て待れけり。少將の立入給ふ姿を一目見て、「命あれば」と計ぞのたまひける。引被てぞ臥給ふ。宰相の内の女房侍共さしつどひて、皆悦び泣共しけり。増て少將の北の方、乳母の六條が心の中、さこそは嬉しかりけめ。六條は盡せぬ物思ひに黒かりし髮も皆白く成り、北の方、さしも花やかにうつくしう坐しか共、いつしか痩衰へて、其人とも見え給はず。少將の流され給し時、三歳にて別給し稚き人、長う成て髮結ふ程也。又其傍に三つ計なる少き人の坐けるを、少將「あれは如何に。」と宣へば、六條「是こそ」とばかり申て、袖を顏におし當て、涙を流しけるにこそ、「さては下りし時、心苦げなる有樣を見置しが、事故なく育けるよ。」と思出ても悲かりけり。少將は本の如く院に召仕はれて、宰相中將にあがり給ふ。

annotation.translation: The Shōshō went to his father-in-law's residence, the Taji no Dainagon. The Shōshō's mother was residing at Reizan, but since yesterday she had been sitting at the Dainagon's residence waiting. When she saw the Shōshō enter, she said, "If he is alive," and then lay down, pulling a cover over herself. The ladies-in-waiting and attendants inside the Dainagon's residence gathered around, all rejoicing and weeping together. Moreover, the Shōshō's lady of the North, the wet nurse Rokujō, must have been exceedingly joyful. Rokujō, who had been consumed by endless worries, had all her black hair turn white; although the lady of the North had once sat so beautifully and radiantly, she had gradually grown thin and frail, and no longer resembled herself. When the Shōshō was exiled, they parted when he was three years old, a young child; now he had grown up and was old enough to have his hair styled. Also sitting nearby was a small child of only three years. When the Shōshō asked, "Who is that?" Rokujō merely said, "It is none other than...", pressed her sleeve to her face, and shed tears. Thinking, "So then, when he departed, I had left him in a sorrowful state, yet he has been raised without any incident," she felt deep sorrow. The Shōshō was summoned back to the Imperial Court as before, and the Dainagon rose to the rank of Chūnagon.

text: 去程に鬼界島へ三人流されたりし流人二人は召還され都へ上りぬ。俊寛僧都一人、憂かりし島の島守と成にけるこそうたてけれ。僧都の、少うより不便にして召仕はれける童あり。名をば有王とぞ申ける。鬼界島の流人、今日既に京都へ入と聞えしかば、鳥羽まで行向うて見けれ共、我主は見え給はず。「如何に」と問へば、「其は猶罪深しとて、島に殘され給ぬ。」と聞て、心憂なども愚也。常は六波羅邊にたゝずみありいて聞けれども、赦免有るべし共聞出ず。僧都の御娘の忍びて坐ける所へ參て、「此せにも洩させ給て、御上りも候はず。如何にもして彼島へ渡て、御行へを尋參らせんとこそ思立て候へ。御文賜はらん。」と申ければ、泣々書て賜だりけり。暇を請共、よも赦さじとて、父にも母にも知せず。唐船の纜は、卯月五月にも解なれば、夏衣立を遲くや思けん。三月の末に都を出て、多くの波路を凌つゝ、薩摩潟へぞ下りける。薩摩より彼島へ渡る船津にて、人怪み、著たる物を剥取などしけれ共、少しも後悔せず、姫御前の御文計ぞ人に見せじとて、髻結の中に隱したり。さて商人船に乘て件の島へ渡て見に、都にて幽に傳聞しは、事の數にもあらず。田もなし。畑もなし。村もなし。里もなし。自ら人は有共、言ふ詞も聞知らず。若しか樣の者共の中に我が主の行末知たる者や在んと、「物申さう」と言ば、「何事」と答ふ。「是に都より流され給し法勝寺執行御房と申す人の、御行末や知たる。」と問に、法勝寺とも執行とも、知たらばこそ返事もせめ。唯頭を掉て「知ず」と言ふ。其中に或者が心得て、「いさとよ、左樣の人は三人是に有しが、二人は召還されて都へ上りぬ。今一人は殘されて、あそこ此に惑ひ歩けども、行方も知らず。」とぞ言ひける。山の方の覺束なさに、遙に分入り、嶺に攀、谷に下れ共、白雲跡を埋んで、往來の道もさだかならず、晴嵐夢を破て其面影も見ざりけり。山にては終に尋も逢はず、海の邊に著て尋るに、沙頭に印を刻む鴎、澳の白洲に集く濱千鳥の外は、跡問ふ者も無りけり。

annotation.translation: Of the three exiles cast away to Kikai Island on the outward journey, the two exiles were summoned back and ascended to the capital. Shunkan Shonyu, however, was left behind to become the island warden of that sorrowful island; this is most grievous. The Shonyu had a young attendant who had been in his service since childhood, who was of humble means. His name was Ario. When it became known that the exiles of Kikai Island had already entered Kyoto today, one went as far as Toba to see them, yet the lord did not deign to appear. When asked, 'How is it?', one replied, 'He is said to remain on the island because his crime is still too great.' Upon hearing this, even one's heart is heavy and sorrowful. Usually, one waits by the Rokuhara side, listening, hoping for a pardon to be granted, yet no such news emerges. One went to the place where the Shonyu's daughter was sitting in secret, saying, 'Even if this secret leaks, and you do not ascend, I intend to do whatever it takes to cross to that island and seek your presence. Please grant me a letter.' When he said this, she wept and wrote one for him. Despite requesting leave, he thought, 'They will never pardon me,' and did not tell his father or mother. When the mooring lines of the Chinese ships are untied in the fifth month of the second lunar month, he wondered if they would delay setting up the summer garments. Leaving the capital at the end of the third month, navigating through many stormy seas, he descended to the Satsuma Lagoon. At the ferry crossing from Satsuma to that island, people suspected him and stripped him of his clothing, yet he felt no regret whatsoever; he thought, 'Only the lady's letter must not be shown to anyone,' and hid it within his topknot. Then, boarding a merchant's ship and crossing to the said island to look, what was heard in the capital as a rumor was nothing compared to the reality. There were no rice fields. No dry fields. No villages. No hamlets. Even if people were present, no words could be heard. If among such people there were any who knew the fate of my lord, and said, 'Let me tell you something,' one would ask, 'What is it?' and reply, 'Do you know the fate of a certain monk named Hossanji no Shugo?' Upon asking, if they knew of Hossanji or Shugo, they would surely respond. Instead, they merely shook their heads and said, 'I do not know.' Among them, one person understood and said, 'Hey, hey, such people are three here; two have been summoned back and ascended to the capital. Now one remains, wandering here and there, yet his whereabouts are unknown.' Due to the indistinctness of the mountain side, he wandered far, climbing ridges and descending valleys, but white clouds filled the tracks, and the path of travel was uncertain; breaking the dreamlike mist, he could not see even its shadow. In the mountains, he finally found no trace or person; going to the seaside and searching, besides the gulls carving prints on the sandy shores and the beach plovers gathering on the white sands of the deep inlet, there was no one left to inquire about traces.

text:
或朝磯の方より、蜻蛉などの樣に痩衰たる者一人よろぼひ出來り。本は法師にて有けりと覺て、髮は虚樣へ生あがり、萬の藻屑取附て、荊を戴たるが如し。節見れて皮ゆたひ、身に著たる物は絹、布の分も見えず。片手には荒海布を拾ひ持ち、片手には網人に魚を貰て持ち、歩む樣にはしけれ共、はかも行かず、よろ／＼として出來たり。
「都にて多くの乞丐人見しか共、かゝる者をば未見ず、『諸阿修羅等故在大海邊』と
て、修羅の三惡四趣は深山大海の邊に有と、佛の説置給ひたれば、知らず、我餓鬼道
に尋來るか。」と思ふほどに、彼も此も次第に歩近づく「若か樣の者も、我主の御行
末知たる事や在ん。」と、「物申さう。」と言ば「何事」と答ふ。「是に都より流さ
れ給し法勝寺の執行御房と申す人の御行末や知たる。」と問に、童は見忘たれ共、僧
都は何か忘べきなれば、「是こそ其よ。」と云も敢ず、手に持る物を投捨て、沙の上
に倒伏す。さてこそ我主の行末も知てけれ。軈て消入給ふを、膝の上に掻乘奉り「有
王が參て候。多くの浪路を凌て、是迄尋參りたる甲斐もなく、いかに軈て憂目をば見
せさせ給ふぞ。」と、泣々申ければ、良在て、少し人心地出來、扶起されて「誠に汝
が是まで尋來たる志の程こそ神妙なれ。明ても暮ても、都の事のみ思ひ居たれば、戀
き者共が面影は、夢に見る折も有り、幻に立つ時も有り。身も痛く疲弱て後は、夢も
現も思分かず。されば汝が來れるも唯夢とのみこそ覺れ。若この事夢ならば、覺ての
後は如何せん。」有王、「現にて候也。此有樣にて、今まで御命の延させ給て候こそ。
不思議には覺候へ。」と申せば、「さればこそ。去年少將や判官入道に棄られて後の便無さ、心の中をば只推量るべし。その瀬に身をも投げんとせしを、由なき少將の、『今一度都の音信をも待かし。』など、慰置しを、愚に若やと頼つゝ、存へんとはせしかども、此島には人の食物絶て無き所なれば、身に力の有し程は、山に上て硫黄と云ふ物をとり、九國より通ふ商人にあひ、物に換などせしかども、日に副て弱行ば、今は其態もせず。か樣に日の長閑なる時は、磯に出て網人釣人に手を摺り、膝を屈て、魚を貰ひ、汐干の時は貝を拾ひ、荒海布を取り、磯の苔に露の命を懸てこそ、今日までも存たれ。さらでは憂世を渡よすがをば、如何にしつらんとか思らん。」僧都、「是にて何事をも言ばやとは思共、いざ我家へ。」と宣へば、此御有樣にても、家を持給へる不思議さよ。」と思て行程に、松の一村ある中に、より竹を柱とし、蘆を結て、桁梁に渡し、上にも下にも松の葉をひしと取懸たれば、風雨たまるべうも無し。昔は法勝寺の寺務職にて、八十餘箇所の庄務を司りしかば、棟門平門の内に、四五百人の所從眷屬に圍繞せられてこそ坐せしか。目のあたりかゝる憂目を見給けるこそ不思議なれ。業にさま／＼あり。順現、順生、順後業と云へり。僧都一期の間、身に用る所、皆大伽藍の寺物佛物にあらずと云ふ事なし。去れば彼信施無慚の罪に依て、今生にはや感ぜられけりとぞ見えたりける。

annotation.translation: One morning, a person came forth from the direction of the seashore, emaciated like a dragonfly. Recognizing him as a priest, his hair stood up as if in a trance, covered with seaweed and debris, resembling someone wearing a crown of thorns. His joints were exposed, and his skin was stretched; no silk or cloth could be seen on his body. In one hand, he held a piece of coarse sea cloth; in the other, a fish given to him by a net-caster. Though he walked with effort, he went no distance, stumbling as he came forward. 'Although I have seen many beggars in the capital, I have never seen anyone like this. "Because of the Asuras, they dwell by the great sea,"' the Buddha taught, saying that the Asuras, the three evil realms and four destinies exist by the deep mountains and great seas. text:
僧都現にて有けりと思定て、「抑去年少將や判官入道が迎にも、是等が文と云ふ事もなし。今汝が便にも、音信の無きはかう共謂ざりけるか。」有王涙に咽び俯して、暫は物も申さず。良有て起上り、涙を抑へて申けるは、「君の西八條へ出させ給しかば、やがて追捕の官人參て、御内の人々搦取り、御謀反の次第を尋て、失果て候ぬ。北方は少き人を隱しかねまゐらせ給ひて、鞍馬の奧に忍ばせ給て候しに、此童計こそ時々參て宮仕つかまつり候しが、何も御歎の愚なる事は候はざりしかども、稚き人は、餘に戀參させ給て、參り候度毎に、『有王よ、鬼界が島とかやへ我具して參れ。』とむづからせ給候しが、過候し二月に、もがさと申す事に失させ給ぬ。北方は其歎と申し是の御事と申し、一方ならぬ御思に沈ませ給ひ、日に添へて弱らせ給候しが、同三月二日の日遂にはかなく成せ給ぬ。今は姫御前ばかり、奈良の姨御前の御許に御渡り候。是に御文賜はて候。」とて取出いて奉る。開て見給へば、有王が申にたがはず書れたり。奧には、「などや三人流されたる人の、二人は召還されて候に、今迄御上り候はぬぞ。哀高きも卑きも、女の身ばかり心うかりける物はなし。男の身にて候はば、渡せ給ふ島へも、などか尋ね參らで候ふべき。此有王御伴にて、急ぎ上せ給へ。」とぞ書かれたる。「是見よ、有王。此子が文の書樣のはかなさよ。己を伴にて、急ぎ上れと書たるこそ恨しけれ。心に任せたる俊寛が身ならば、何とてか三年の春秋をば送るべき。今年は十二に成とこそ思に、是程はかなくては、人にも見え、宮仕をもして、
身をも扶くべきか。」とて泣れけるにこそ、人の親の心は闇にあらね共、子を思ふ道
に迷ふ程も知れけれ。「此島へ流されて後は、暦も無れば月日の換り行をも知らず、
唯自ら花の散り、葉の落るを見て、春秋を辨へ、蝉の聲麥秋を送れば夏と思ひ、雪の積を冬と知る。白月黒月の變行を見ては、三十日を辨へ、指を折て數れば、今年は六に成と思つる稚き者も早先立けるごさんなれ。西八條へ出し時、此子が我も行うと慕しを、軈て歸うずるぞと拵へ置しが、今の樣に覺るぞや。其を限と思はましかば、今暫もなどか見ざらん。親と成り、子と成り、夫婦の縁を結も、皆此世一に限ぬ契ぞかし。などさらば、其等が左樣に先立けるを、今迄夢幻にも知せざりけるぞ。人目も愧ず如何にもして、命生うと思しも、是等を今一度見ばやと思ふ爲也。姫が事計こそ心苦けれ共、其も生身なれば、歎ながらも過んずらん。さのみ存て、己に憂目を見せんも我身ながらも強顏かるべし。」とて、自らの食事を止め、偏に彌陀の名號を唱へて、臨終正念をぞ祈られける。有王渡て廿三日と云に、其庵の内にて遂に終り給ぬ。歳三十七とぞ聞えし。有王空き姿に取附き、天に仰ぎ地に俯し、泣悲め共かひぞなき。心の行程泣あきて、「軈て後世の御供仕るべう候へども、此世には姫御前ばかりこそ御渡候へ。後世弔ひまゐらすべき人も候はず。暫存て、弔ひ參せ候はんとて、臥戸を改めず、庵を切懸け、松の枯枝、蘆の枯葉を取掩ひ、藻鹽の煙と成し奉り、荼毘事終にければ、白骨を拾ひ、頸に懸け、又商人船の便に、九國の地へぞ著にける。

annotation.translation: The monk Sozu, having come, thought, 'I believe he is here,' and said, 'In the first place, last year, when the Shōshō and the Danjō Nyūdō came to meet, there was not even such a thing as a letter from them. Now, even if you have a messenger, the fact that there is no word from them—was it not said so?' Prince Ariō, choking with tears and bowing his head, said nothing for a while. Yoshinari rose, suppressing his tears, and said, 'When your lordship was dispatched to Saishōjō, immediately the officials of pursuit came, apprehended the people within the palace, inquired into the details of the alleged rebellion, and lost all hope. Your lordship, fearing that few people would be able to hide him, secretly sent him to the depths of Kurama, where this child, who was always coming and serving the court, did not do anything particularly worthy of your lordship's sorrow. Yet, the young one, longing for you too much, whenever he came, would say, "Ariō, go to the Island of the Netherworld with me." But in the second month that passed, he was lost in the matter of "Mogasato." Your lordship, hearing of this sorrow and this matter, sank into a strange grief, and day by day grew weaker. Finally, on the second day of the third month, he passed away. Now, only Princess Himemae has been transferred to the house of the aunt in Nara. This is written in the letter I present.' He opened it and read it. It was written exactly as Ariō had said. In the margin was written: 'Why have the three exiles been cast away? Two have been summoned back, yet you have not come up until now. Whether high or low, there is no one whose heart is lighter than a woman's. If one were a man, how could one fail to inquire and go to the island to which one was sent? Come quickly with this Ariō.' "Look at this, Ariō. How fragile is the handwriting of this child's letter! He wrote that I should accompany him and come quickly; this is truly bitter. If it were Shunkan, who followed his own heart, how could he have spent three years of spring and autumn? I thought this year I would turn twelve, but how can I, who am so frail, be seen by others, serve the court, and support my own body?" He said, and wept. Indeed, the heart of a parent is not dark, yet it is known that one can become lost in the path of thinking of one's child. "Since being exiled to this island, there is no calendar, and I do not know the changing of months and days. I only watch the flowers fall and the leaves drop to distinguish the seasons; when I hear the sound of cicadas and send off the wheat harvest, I think it is summer; when snow piles up, I know it is winter. Watching the changes of the white moon and the black moon, I count thirty days and, by counting on my fingers, think this year I have turned twelve, and the young one has grown up so quickly. When you were dispatched to Saishōjō, this child longed to go with me, and I prepared him to return soon, but I did not expect him to wake up like this. If I had thought of this as a limit, how could I not have seen him for even a short time? Becoming a parent, becoming a child, forming the bond of husband and wife—all are contracts limited to this world only. Why, then, did I not know until now that they had passed away, not even in a dream? Out of shame before the eyes of men, I thought of doing anything and even of keeping my life, but I wish to see them once more. The matter of the princess is indeed distressing, yet since she is of flesh and blood, she will surely pass away even with sorrow. Thus thinking, even if I must look upon myself with a sad face, I, as my own body, must put on a strong face." He said, stopped his own meal, and alone chanted the name of Amida, praying for the correct thought at the moment of death. After Ariō crossed over and twenty-three days had passed, he finally passed away within that hut. It is said he was thirty-seven years old. Ariō, in his empty state, clung to him, looked up to heaven and bowed down to the earth, weeping bitterly, but it was of no avail. His heart's journey, exhausted by tears, said, 'Soon I shall serve you in the next world, but in this world, only Princess Himemae has been transferred. There is no one to perform mourning rites in the next world. For a while, I shall remain and perform the rites,' so he did not change the sliding door, left the hut as it was, gathered withered pine branches and withered reed leaves, turned them into smoke of seaweed salt, and when the cremation was finished, he picked up the white bones, hung them around his neck, and again, taking advantage of a merchant's boat, arrived in the land of the Nine Provinces.

text: 僧都の御女の座ける處に參て、有し樣初より細々と語申す。「中々文を御覽じてこそ、いとゞ御思は勝せ給て候ひしか。硯も紙も候はねば、御返事にも及ばず。思召され候し御心の中、さながら空て止候にき。今は生々世々を送り、他生曠劫を隔つ共、爭か御聲をも聞き、御姿をも見參せ給べき。」と申ければ、伏轉び聲も惜ず泣かれけり。軈て十二の歳尼になり、奈良の法華寺に行澄て、父母の後世を弔ひ給ぞ哀なる。有王は俊寛僧都の遺骨を頸にかけ、高野へ登り、奧の院に納つゝ、蓮華谷にて法師になり、諸國七道修行して、主の後世をぞ弔ける。か樣に人の思歎の積ぬる平家の末こそ怖しけれ。

annotation.translation: He approached the place where the Nun of the Monk-Abbot was seated, and began to speak in detail from the beginning about his situation. 'It is only by your having read this letter that I am all the more grateful to you. Since I have neither an inkstone nor paper, I cannot even write a reply. I fear that the mind you have kindly conceived has, as it were, come to a standstill in vain. Now, while we live out this life and the next, even if we are separated across countless eons, how can I ever hope to hear your voice or see your countenance?' When he said this, she fell prostrate and wept without sparing her voice. Soon she became a nun at the age of twelve, went to the Hokke-ji Temple in Nara, and there performed rites for the afterlife of her parents; how pitiful it was. Arimori placed the remains of Monk-Abbot Shunkan around his neck, climbed to Koya, and as he was enshrining them in the Oku-no-in, he became a monk at Renge Valley, undertook pilgrimages throughout the seven provinces, and performed rites for the afterlife of his lord. Thus, it is truly fearful to see the descendants of the Taira clan, whose hearts are piled with the sighs and sorrows of men.

text: 同五月十二日午刻ばかり、京中には辻風おびたゞしう吹て、人屋多く顛倒す。風は中御門京極より起て、未申の方へ吹て行に、棟門平門を吹拔きて、四五町十町吹もて行き、桁長押柱などは虚空に散在す。檜皮、葺板の類、冬の木の葉の風に亂るが如し。おひたゞしう鳴どよむ音は、彼地獄の業風なり共、是には過じとぞ見えし。唯舎屋の破損する耳ならず、命を失ふ人も多し。牛馬の類數を盡して打殺さる。是たゝ事に非ず。御占有るべしとて、神祇官にして御占有り。「今百日の中に、祿を重ずる大臣の愼、別しては天下の大事、幵に佛法王法共に傾きて、兵革相續すべし。」とぞ、神祇官陰陽寮ともに占ひ申ける。

annotation.translation: On the twelfth day of the fifth month, around noon, a wind of terrible violence blew through Kyoto, overturning many houses. The wind arose from the Nakamikado-Kyogoku area and blew toward the southwest, stripping the roofs off the gatehouses and the main gates, and blowing on for four or five cho, or even ten cho; the beams, lintels, and pillars were scattered into the empty air. The cypress bark and roof boards were tossed about as if by the winter wind scattering leaves. The deafening roar sounded like the karmic wind of hell, yet it appeared even worse than that. Not only were many houses damaged, but many people also lost their lives. The cattle and horses were killed in great numbers. This was no ordinary occurrence; it was to be divined by the Bureau of Divination. The Bureau of Divination and the Bureau of Onmyo both divined and reported: "Within the next hundred days, the ministers, who should be cautious in their duties, will fail; especially, the great affairs of the realm will collapse, and Buddhism and secular law will both fall, and warfare will continue."

text:
小松大臣、か樣の事共を聞給て、萬心細うや思はれけん。其比熊野參詣の事有けり。
本宮證誠殿の御前にて、終夜敬白せられけるは、「親父入道相國の體を見るに、惡逆
無道にして、動すれば君を惱し奉る。重盛長子として、頻に諫をいたすと云へども、身不肖の間、彼以て服膺せず。其振舞を見るに一期の榮華猶危し。枝葉連續して、親を現し名を揚ん事難し。此時に當て、重盛苟うも思へり。憖に列して、世に浮沈せん事、敢て良臣孝子の法に非ず。しかじ、名を遁れ身を退て、今生の名望を投捨て、來世の菩提を求んには。但凡夫薄地、是非に惑るが故に、猶志を恣にせず。南無權現金剛童子、願くは子孫榮絶えずして、仕て朝廷に交はるべくば、入道の惡心を和て、天下の安全を得しめ給へ。榮耀又一期を限て、後昆耻に及ぶべくば、重盛が運命をつゞめて、來世の苦輪を助け給へ。兩箇の求願、偏に冥助を仰ぐ。」と、肝膽を摧て祈念せられけるに、燈籠の火の樣なる物の、大臣の御身より出て、はと消るが如くして失にけり。人數多見奉りけれども、恐れて是を申さず。

annotation.translation: The Minister Komatsu, having heard of the various matters concerning the lady, felt his heart to be extremely uneasy. At that time, there was an event regarding a pilgrimage to Kumano. Before the main hall of the Shōshōden, he devoted himself throughout the night in solemn prayer: 'My father, the Monk, in his nature, is wicked, rebellious, and unjust; whatever he does causes distress to the Sovereign. As his eldest son, I have frequently offered admonitions, yet, being unworthy, he has not accepted them. Witnessing his conduct, even this present glory is precarious. To continue the lineage and to bring honor to my parents is difficult. At this moment, I, Shigemori, have considered this: to remain in the world and experience its rise and fall is not in accordance with the principles of a loyal minister and a filial son. Therefore, to escape from my name and withdraw from my position, casting aside my reputation in this life and seeking enlightenment in the next—yet, being a mere mortal with shallow understanding, I am confused by right and wrong, and thus I cannot freely determine my will. O Namu Gonkin Kongō Dōji, I pray that if my descendants may prosper without end and serve the Imperial Court, may you soothe the monk's wicked heart and grant safety to the realm. If glory is limited to this one generation and brings shame to future generations, may you, Shigemori, take my fate upon yourself and relieve the suffering of the wheel of rebirth in the next life. These two prayers are solely placed in the hands of the unseen powers.' Having prayed with a heart broken to its core, a light resembling a lantern flame emerged from the Minister's body and vanished instantly, like a bird flying away. Many people witnessed it, yet they dared not speak of it.

text:
又下向の時、岩田河を渡られけるに、嫡子權亮少將維盛已下の公達、淨衣の下に薄色の衣を著て、夏の事なれば、何となう河の水に戯れ給ふ程に、淨衣のぬれて衣に移たるが、偏に色の如くに見ければ、筑後守貞能是を見咎て、「何と候やらん、あの御淨衣の世に忌はしきやうに見させ座し候。召替らるべうや候らん。」と申されければ、
大臣「我所願既に成就しにけり。其淨衣敢て改むべからず。」とて、別して岩田河よ
り、熊野へ悦の奉幣をぞ立られける。人怪しと思ひけれ共、其心を得ず。然に此公達、
程なく、誠の色を著給けるこそ不思議なれ。

annotation.translation: Again, when he went down to the provinces, as he was crossing the Iwata River, the courtiers including the legitimate heir, Gonryo Shosho Tairano no Morimori, wearing thin-colored garments under their white ceremonial robes, and since it was summer, while they were playfully splashing in the river water, the white robes became wet and the thin-colored garments showed through, which appeared exactly as they had feared. Tsukushi no Kami Sane'no then reprimanded them, saying, 'What is going on? You have made that sacred white robe appear so abominable in the world. Should it not be changed?' Upon hearing this, the Minister said, 'My wish has already been fulfilled. That sacred white robe must not be altered at all.' Then, parting ways, they set out from the Iwata River to present the ceremonial offerings at Kumano with joy. Although the people found it strange, they could not comprehend his heart. Yet, it was indeed strange that these courtiers, without delay, were wearing the color of sincerity.

text: 下向の後幾くの日數を經ずして、病附給ふ。權現既に御納受あるにこそとて、療治もしたまはず。祈祷をも致されず。其比宋朝より勝たる名醫渡て、本朝にやすらふ事あり。境節入道相國、福原の別業に座けるが、越中守盛俊を使で、小松殿へ仰られけるは、「所勞彌大事なる由、其聞え有り。兼ては又宋朝より勝たる名醫渡れり。境節悦とす。是を召請じて醫療を加しめ給へ。」と、宣遣はされたりければ、小松殿扶起され、盛俊を御前へ召て「先醫療の事、畏て承候ぬと申べし。但汝も承れ。延喜の御門は、さばかの賢王にて渡せまし／＼けれ共、異國の相人を都の内へ入させ給たりけるをば、末代迄も賢王の御誤、本朝の耻とこそ見えたれ。況や重盛程の凡人が、異國の醫師を王城へ入ん事、國の耻に非ずや。漢高祖は、三尺の劔を提て天下を治しかども、淮南の黥布を討し時、流矢に當て疵を蒙る。后呂太后、良醫を迎て見せしむるに、醫の曰く『此疵治しつべし。但五十斤の金を與へば治せん。』と云ふ。高祖のたまはく、『我守の強かし程は、多くの鬪に逢て疵を蒙りしか共、其痛無し。運既に盡ぬ。命は則天に在り。縱ひ扁鵲といふとも、何の益か有ん。然ば又金を惜に似たり。』とて、五十斤の金を醫師に與へながら遂に治せざりき。先言耳に在り、今以て甘心す。重盛苟も九卿に列し、三台に昇る。その運命を計るに、もて天心に在り。何ぞ天心を察せずして、愚に醫療を痛はしうせむや。若定業たらば醫療を加ふ共益無からんか。又非業たらば、療治をくはへず共、助る事を得べし。彼耆婆が醫術及ばずして、大覺世尊、滅度を跋提河の邊に唱ふ。是即定業の病、いやさざる事を示さんが爲也。定業猶醫療に拘るべう候はば、釋尊豈入滅あらんや。定業又治するに堪ざる旨明し。治するは佛體也。療するは耆婆也。然れば重盛が身佛體に非ず。名醫又耆婆に及べからず。縱四部の書を鑑て、百療に長ずといふ共、爭で有待の穢身を求療せんや。縱五經の説を詳にして、衆病をいやすと云共、豈前世の業病を治せんや。若かの醫術に依て存命せば、本朝の醫道無に似たり。醫術効驗なくんば、面謁所詮なし。就中に本朝鼎臣の外相を以て、異朝浮遊の來客に見ん事、且は國の耻、且は道の陵遲也。縱重盛命は亡ずといふ共、爭か國の恥を思ふ心を存ぜざらん。此由を申せ。」とこそ宣ひけれ。

annotation.translation: Shortly after his departure, he fell ill. Though the Gongen had already been received, no treatment was administered, nor was any prayer offered. At that time, a renowned physician from the Song Dynasty crossed over and was residing in our country. The monk Saigetsu, who was the Chancellor and was residing at the detached villa in Fukuhara, sent Mototoshi, the Governor of Echigo, to the residence of the Lord Komatsu, saying, 'It is reported that your illness is extremely serious. Moreover, a renowned physician from the Song Dynasty has crossed over. Saigetsu rejoices in this. Please summon him and have him administer medical treatment.' When this message was conveyed, the Lord Komatsu rose, summoned Mototoshi before him, and said, 'You should say that I have previously received your message regarding medical treatment with due reverence. However, you too should understand. The Imperial House of Enki, though it was led by wise kings who were wise, allowed a foreign physiognomist to enter the capital; this is seen as a mistake of the wise king and a disgrace to our nation that has lasted to the present age. How much more so, for a commoner like Shigemori to allow a foreign physician into the royal capital—would this not be a disgrace to the nation? Gaozu of the Han Dynasty, though he wielded a three-foot sword to govern the realm, when he fought against the rebel Ying Bu of Huainan, was struck by a stray arrow and suffered a wound. Later Empress Lu welcomed a physician and showed him the wound; the physician said, 'This wound can be cured, but if fifty jin of gold are given, it will be cured.' Gaozu replied, 'The strength of my constitution is such that I have encountered many battles and suffered wounds, yet I have felt no pain. My fate is already exhausted. My life lies in Heaven's will. Even if Bian Que were to come, what benefit would he bring? Therefore, I am reluctant to part with the gold.' Thus, although he gave fifty jin of gold to the physician, he was never cured. The words I spoke before are now in my ears, and I am now content. Shigemori, though he has been listed among the Nine Ministers and has ascended to the Three High Posts, his fate lies in the will of Heaven. Why would one, without understanding the will of Heaven, foolishly insist on medical treatment? If it is one's predetermined fate, even if medical treatment is administered, it will be of no benefit. If it is not one's predetermined fate, even if medical treatment is not added, one may still be saved. The physician Jivaka could not cure [the Buddha], and the Great Sage World Honored One proclaimed Nirvana by the side of the River Bodhi. This is to show that the illness of predetermined fate cannot be cured. If one were to be bound by medical treatment regarding predetermined fate, would the Buddha have entered Nirvana? The fact that predetermined fate cannot be cured is clearly shown. To cure is the body of the Buddha; to treat is Jivaka. Therefore, Shigemori's body is not the body of the Buddha. Even a renowned physician cannot surpass Jivaka. Even if one examines the Four Treatises and is skilled in a hundred cures, how can one seek treatment for a body defiled by waiting? Even if one elaborates on the theories of the Five Classics and claims to cure all diseases, how can one cure the disease of karma from a previous life? If, relying on such medical techniques, one were to prolong life, the medical tradition of our nation would be as good as nothing. If medical techniques lack efficacy, there is no point in an audience. Especially, for a high minister of our nation to be seen as a wandering guest from a foreign dynasty, this is both a disgrace to the nation and a decline of the Way. Even if Shigemori's life were not lost, how could one not feel the thought of the nation's disgrace? Thus, I have spoken these words.'

text: 盛俊福原に歸りまゐて、此由泣々申ければ、入道相國、「是程國の恥を思ふ大臣上古にも未聞かず、増て末代に有べし共覺えず。日本に相應せぬ大臣なれば、如何樣にも今度失なんず。」とて、泣く／＼急ぎ都へ上られけり。

annotation.translation: Motonori returned to Fuhara and, weeping, reported these events; the Dajō-daijin said, "A minister who thinks of the disgrace of the nation to this extent has never been heard of since ancient times, nor is there any sign of such a thing in future generations. Since he is a minister unworthy of Japan, he will surely lose his position this time." And so, weeping, he hurriedly ascended to the capital.

text: 同七月廿八日小松殿出家し給ぬ。法名は淨蓮とこそつき給へ。やがて八月一日、臨終正念に住して遂に失給ぬ。御歳四十三、世は盛とこそ見えつるに、哀なりし事共也。

annotation.translation: On the 28th day of the same seventh month, Lord Komatsu entered religious life. His priestly name was bestowed as Joren. Soon, on the first day of the eighth month, he dwelt in right mindfulness at the time of death and finally passed away. He was forty-three years of age; the world seemed flourishing, yet what a sorrowful thing it was.

text: 入道相國の、さしも横紙をやられつるも、此人のなほし宥られつればこそ、世も穩かりつれ。此後天下に如何なる事か出來んずらむとて、京中の上下歎合へり。前右大將宗盛卿の方樣の人は、世は唯今大將殿へ參りなんずとぞ悦ける。人の親の子を思ふ習は、愚なるが先立だにも悲きぞかし。況や是は當家の棟梁當世の賢人にておはしければ、恩愛の別、家の衰微、悲でも猶餘有り。去ば世には良臣を失へる事を歎き、家には武略の廢ぬる事を悲む。凡は此大臣文章麗うして、心に忠を存し、才藝勝て、詞に徳を兼給へり。

annotation.translation: The fact that the Dajō-daijin (Minister of State) had also been so severely punished was precisely because this person had been still further pardoned, and thus the world had become stable. Worrying that something might happen to the realm from now on, all in Kyoto, from high to low, sighed in unison. The people of the side of the former Right Great General, Sōmori-no-Kyō, rejoiced, saying, 'The world is now going to His Excellency the Great General.' The habit of parents thinking of their children is sorrowful even for the foolish beforehand. How much more so when this is the head of the house and a wise man of the present age; the parting of affection and the decline of the family bring sorrow, yet there is still more to be mourned. Thus, the world laments the loss of a loyal minister, and the house mourns the abandonment of military strategy. In general, this Great Minister was beautiful in his writings, kept loyalty in his heart, excelled in talent and art, and bestowed virtue in his words.

text: 天性此大臣は、不思議の人にて、未來の事をも兼て悟給けるにや、去四月七日の夢に、見給ける事こそ不思議なれ。譬ば、何く共知らぬ濱路を遙々と歩行給ふ程に、道の傍に大なる鳥居有けるを、「あれは如何なる鳥居やらん。」と問給へば、「春日大明神の御鳥居なり。」と申。人多く群集したり。其中に、法師の頭を一つ指擧たり。「さてあのくびは如何に。」と問給へば、是は平家太政入道殿の御頭を惡行超過し給へるに依て、當社大明神の召取せ給て候。」と申と覺えて、夢打覺ぬ。當家は保元平治より以降、度々の朝敵を平げて、勸賞身に餘り、忝く一天の君の御外戚として、一族の昇進六十餘人。二十餘年の以降は、樂榮え申計も無りつるに、入道の惡行超過せるに依て、一門の運命既に盡んずるにこそと、こし方行末の事共思召續けて、御涙に咽ばせ給ふ。

annotation.translation: This minister was naturally a strange person, and perhaps he also foresaw future events; indeed, what he saw in his dream on the seventh day of the fourth month was truly remarkable. For instance, as he was walking far along a beach he had never known before, he noticed a large torii gate by the road. When he asked, 'What kind of torii gate is that?', he was told, 'It is the sacred torii gate of Kasuga Taisha.' Many people were gathered there. Among them, a monk pointed up at one severed head. When he asked, 'What shall we do with that neck?', he was told, 'Because Lord Dajō-daijin Taira no Kiyomori committed such egregious evil deeds, the god of this shrine has summoned his head.' Upon waking from the dream with this recollection, he awoke. From the times of the Hōgen and Heiji rebellions onward, this house had repeatedly pacified rebels who rose against the imperial court, and the rewards bestowed upon it were far beyond its due; shamefully, as the maternal kin of the Emperor, it had enjoyed the advancement of over sixty members of its clan. Yet for more than twenty years, no joy had been experienced. However, because of the egregious evil deeds committed by the retired minister, it is felt that the fate of the entire clan has already come to an end; thus, he continued to ponder the future of his lineage and the course of events, and he was made to choke with tears.

text: 折節妻戸をほと／＼と打敲く。「誰そ。あれ聞。」と宣へば、「瀬尾太郎兼康が參て候。」と申。「如何に、何事ぞ。」とのたまへば、「只今、不思議の事候て、夜の明候はんが遲う覺え候間、申さんが爲に參て候。御前の人を除られ候へ。」と申ければ、大臣人を遙に除て對面あり。さて兼康が見たりける夢の樣を始より終まで委しう語り申けるが、大臣の御覽じたりける御夢に少しも違はず。さてこそ瀬尾太郎兼康をば、神にも通じたる者にてありけりと大臣も感じ給ひけれ。

annotation.translation: Just then, someone knocked on the wife's door repeatedly. 'Who is it? Come and listen,' he said. 'Seo no Taro Kaneyasu has come,' he replied. 'What is it? What is the matter?' he asked. 'Just now, something strange happened; it seems that dawn is late, so I have come to report it. Please have everyone else withdraw from your presence,' he said. The Minister therefore had his attendants withdraw far away and received Kaneyasu in audience. Then Kaneyasu recounted the dream he had seen in full detail from beginning to end, and it differed not at all from the dream the Minister had seen. Then the Minister also felt that Seo no Taro Kaneyasu must indeed be someone who could communicate with the gods.
